paper.title: Algorithm 875: DSDP5, software for semidefinite programming
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 34(3), Article 16 (May 2008) (TOMS 875)

code.note: C library with examples. The example driver examples/theta.c (built as theta, through the examples Makefile against the library in src/) reads a graph, forms the Lovasz theta SDP, and prints the solver log. bin/Makefile target thetatest runs 'theta graph1' and diffs the log against bin/output.theta; bin/graph1 is the 6-node, 8-edge input (shipped, no download needed). The shipped reference log is bin/output.theta, whose last line is iteration 4 with the DD Objective -3.00000012e+00.

claim.location: The shipped reference log bin/output.theta (member of 875.zip), final iteration line (iteration 4) of the 'theta graph1' run: DD Objective -3.00000012e+00 (the Lovasz theta value of graph1 up to the sign convention of the printed log; the PP Objective on the same line is -2.99983133e+00).
claim.metric: The DD Objective of the last iteration in the theta graph1 run, compared as an absolute value: |DD| against 3.00000012.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read in this wake; the value is taken from the shipped reference log.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The solver stops when its duality gap is about 1e-7 (last Nu 5.6e-08 in the reference log), so the objective is fixed to about 1e-7 by the algorithm. 1e-5 absorbs platform and compiler rounding in the last digits of an interior-point run, and is far tighter than the 2-3 unit spread between iterations. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: build the C library and the theta example with the shipped Makefiles, then one run on a 6-node graph.
cost.data_size: None beyond the archive (bin/graph1 ships in the archive).
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic interior-point SDP solve whose converged optimum is printed in a shipped reference log; the number is the output of a computation the code must run (Lovasz theta of a small graph), not a closed form for this graph.
